summary.title: pfsense-siem-stack
summary.description: Threat model of the pfSense Suricata/pfBlockerNG to Logstash/OpenSearch/Grafana stack as built by setup.sh, install.sh and the forwarder. Public. No LLM component. Doc-only items are marked UNVERIFIED.

data.description: Sources of the traffic Suricata inspects. Everything here is attacker-controllable.

data.name: Internet and LAN hosts

threats.title: Event flood hides real attacks
threats.description: An attacker can generate enough alerts to saturate the single-socket UDP forwarder and the Logstash UDP buffer (config/logstash-suricata.conf sets a 32 MB receive buffer; forwarder sends datagrams with no ack, no retry and no queue: forward-suricata-eve.py:tail_log_file). Dropped datagrams are silent. On restart the forwarder seeks to end of file (f.seek(0,2)), so events during a restart are not forwarded.

data.name: Operator (admin)
data.description: Runs setup.sh, install.sh and the pfsense-siem console; browses Grafana.

data.name: Rule and feed providers
data.description: Suricata rule sources and pfBlockerNG feeds. UNVERIFIED: only documented (docs/pfsense/PFBLOCKERNG_FEED_REFERENCE.md, config/sid/README.md); the rule update itself runs inside the pfSense packages, not in this repo.

threats.title: Malicious or mistaken feed or rule update changes blocking behavior
threats.description: UNVERIFIED: depends on pfSense package behavior, not repo code. A compromised feed could block legitimate addresses or enable a rule set that drops legitimate traffic. The repo only ships SID lists (config/sid/drop/dropsid-comprehensive.conf) that convert alert rules to drop in inline IPS mode, which raises false-positive blast radius.

data.name: Package and artifact sources
data.description: artifacts.opensearch.org, artifacts.elastic.co, packages.grafana.com, GitHub (install.sh install_opensearch, install_logstash, install_grafana).

threats.title: OpenSearch tarball installed without checksum or signature check
threats.description: install.sh:install_opensearch downloads opensearch-VERSION-linux-x64.tar.gz over HTTPS with wget and extracts it to /opt/opensearch with no sha256 or signature verification (grep for sha256/gpg --verify finds nothing). Logstash and Grafana come from apt repos with signed-by keyrings, but the keys are fetched over HTTPS at install time (trust on first use). Versions are pinned (OPENSEARCH_VERSION=2.19.4).
threats.mitigation: None in the repository. The tarball download in install.sh install_opensearch is still not verified; not changed in the fix for #49.

data.name: GitHub Actions
data.description: CI and wiki publishing (.github/workflows/ci.yml, security.yml, wiki.yml, dependabot-auto-merge.yml).

threats.title: Workflow supply chain
threats.description: Reusable workflows from ChiefGyk3D/git-your-ship-together are called by full commit SHA with a version comment (ci.yml, security.yml, dependabot-auto-merge.yml), permissions default to contents: read, and ci.yml and security.yml set egress-policy: block.
threats.mitigation: Pinned by SHA with read-only default permissions and egress block: .github/workflows/ci.yml, security.yml. wiki.yml and dependabot-auto-merge.yml request contents: write; wiki.yml pin was not reviewed in depth (NOT VERIFIED).

data.name: Suricata (pfSense package)
data.description: IDS/IPS on pfSense interfaces; writes /var/log/suricata/*/eve.json. The package is not in this repo; repo ships SID lists in config/sid and scripts/apply-suricata-drop-rules.sh.

threats.title: Attacker-triggered false-positive drops
threats.description: UNVERIFIED (inferred from config/sid/drop/dropsid-comprehensive.conf and scripts/apply-suricata-drop-rules.sh): in inline IPS mode, rules converted to drop will drop legitimate flows that match, and an attacker who can make a victim's traffic match a signature can cause an outage for it. apply-suricata-drop-rules.sh hardcodes instance names and copies generated rules without validating them (--no-test).

data.name: EVE forwarder (forward-suricata-eve.py)
data.description: Python daemon on pfSense, started by rc.d script written by setup.sh, daemon -r, watchdog every minute via cron. Tails eve.json, adds GeoIP, sends JSON over UDP.

threats.title: Forwarder runs as root and parses untrusted-influenced JSON
threats.description: The forwarder runs as root (setup.sh watchdog: pgrep -u root; rc.d script). eve.json contains attacker-controlled strings (HTTP host, DNS names, TLS SNI), parsed with json.loads and re-serialized; no eval or shell use was found in forward-suricata-eve.py, which limits this to a latent risk in json/maxminddb parsing. No privilege drop.

threats.title: Log rotation silently stops forwarding
threats.description: tail_log_file detects inode change, truncation and disappearance, and a watchdog restarts the process if it dies.
threats.mitigation: forward-suricata-eve.py:tail_log_file (inode/size checks every ~5 s); setup.sh watchdog + pfSense cron; tests/python/test_forwarder.py exists.

data.name: pfBlockerNG
data.description: pfSense package producing ip_block.log and dnsbl.log. UNVERIFIED: only documented (docs/pfsense/TELEGRAF_PFBLOCKER_SETUP.md); no repo code configures it.

data.name: Telegraf + repo plugins
data.description: Telegraf on pfSense runs plugins/telegraf_*.php|sh and tails pfBlockerNG logs, outputs to OpenSearch. Runs as root (docs/pfsense/TELEGRAF_ON_PFSENSE.md). Output config lives in config.xml and is UNVERIFIED (documented only).

threats.title: Command injection in Telegraf plugins
threats.description: plugins/telegraf_arp_mac_vendor.php calls shell_exec with a fixed string ('arp -an') and no variable input; output is only parsed.
threats.mitigation: Fixed command string at plugins/telegraf_arp_mac_vendor.php:61. Other plugins (.sh) were skimmed, not audited line by line (NOT VERIFIED).

data.name: Setup deployment on pfSense
data.description: setup.sh pushes forward-suricata-eve.py, a watchdog, an rc.d script and a cron entry to pfSense over SSH as the admin user and starts them as root.

threats.title: Operator workstation or SSH key compromise reaches root code execution on the firewall
threats.description: setup.sh scp's an executable to /usr/local/bin, writes an rc.d script and cron entry through ssh, all run by root. The operator key is the only gate. scripts/preflight.sh uses StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new (trust on first use); setup.sh uses the default host key policy.

data.name: eve.json logs
data.description: /var/log/suricata/*/eve.json on pfSense (read by forwarder). Contains DNS names, HTTP hosts, TLS SNI, flow metadata for monitored users.

data.name: GeoLite2 database
data.description: MaxMind .mmdb files read by the forwarder (paths in forward-suricata-eve.py GEOIP_DB_PATHS). Provenance of the file is out of this repo (docs/install/GEOIP_SETUP.md, not verified).

data.name: Logstash (config/logstash-suricata.conf)
data.description: udp input 5140 -> json filter into [@metadata][eve] -> ruby validation and allow-listed copy to the root (quarantine to eve-quarantine-* on failure) -> date -> time-range check -> opensearch output http://localhost:9200. Installed by install.sh; config pushed by setup.sh.

threats.title: Unauthenticated UDP input: a reachable host can still send well-formed fake events
threats.description: Residual after the t_spoof fix. The udp input on 5140 still has no authentication or integrity, and UDP source addresses can be spoofed by a host on the same segment as the pfSense address allowed by install.sh:configure_firewall (LOGSTASH_ALLOWED_SOURCES). config/logstash-suricata.conf now parses into [@metadata][eve], validates, and copies only allow-listed Suricata keys, so the sender can no longer set @timestamp, @version, tags, host, message or unlisted fields, or pick an arbitrary index date. What remains: a sender can still submit a valid-looking event under the allowed schema (event_type, src_ip, dest_ip, alert.signature, alert.severity, alert.action, in_iface), so it can add fake alerts to the dashboards or flood noise to bury a real one. Severity is Medium, not High: nothing in this repo acts on these events (no Grafana alert rules or automated response were found; scripts/check-telegram-alerts.sh only greps logs), so a forged event can mislead a human or hide a real one but not trigger an action. Also: a flood to the quarantine index costs disk until retention is configured for eve-quarantine-*.
threats.mitigation: Reduced, not closed. Done: field allow-list, type/range/size/depth validation and timestamp range check in the ruby filters of config/logstash-suricata.conf; failing events go to eve-quarantine-* (output branch on [@metadata][quarantine_reason]); tests/python/test_logstash_eve_filter.py runs the ruby under plain ruby (Logstash itself was not run). Source allow-list in install.sh:configure_firewall / firewall_plan (scripts/lib-install-safety.sh). Needed for the residual: a network control that authenticates the path (dedicated VLAN or link between pfSense and the SIEM, or IPsec/WireGuard with Logstash listening only on the tunnel address); documented in docs/reference/CONFIGURATION.md, Sender integrity. UDP syslog cannot authenticate by itself.

threats.title: Malformed input crashes the pipeline
threats.description: Parse failures are tagged _jsonparsefailure and skipped by the date filter; the pipeline continues.
threats.mitigation: config/logstash-suricata.conf filter section (json tag_on_failure, conditional date/mutate).

threats.title: Pipeline file replaced during deployment
threats.description: setup.sh creates the remote temp file with umask 077 mktemp and installs it with sudo install -m 0644 -o root -g root before restarting Logstash.

data.name: OpenSearch 2.19.4
data.description: Single node, HTTP 9200. install.sh writes network.host: 0.0.0.0 and plugins.security.disabled: true. Indexes suricata-* and pfblockerng-*.

threats.title: OpenSearch API has no authentication, TLS or role separation and is opened to all sources
threats.description: install.sh writes opensearch.yml with network.host: 0.0.0.0 and plugins.security.disabled: true and then ufw allow 9200/tcp with no source restriction. Anyone who can route to TCP 9200 can read, modify or delete every index and change cluster settings. This is documented as a known gap in docs/reference/CONFIGURATION.md (Security) and ROADMAP.md, but the installer still applies it. Exploit requires only network reachability.
threats.mitigation: install.sh install_opensearch writes opensearch.yml through render_opensearch_yml (scripts/lib-install-safety.sh): network.host defaults to 127.0.0.1 and a non-loopback OPENSEARCH_BIND is refused unless OPENSEARCH_ALLOWED_SOURCES and OPENSEARCH_DISABLE_SECURITY=true are set. install.sh configure_firewall uses firewall_plan, which adds no 9200 rule for a loopback bind and a source-limited rule otherwise. The old open install needs INSECURE_OPEN_ACCESS=true (documented in config.env.example). Residual: the security plugin is still disabled (no authentication or TLS) and existing installs keep their old opensearch.yml and ufw rules; install.sh warns. Checked by tests/python/test_install_safety.py.

threats.title: No audit trail of who read or changed data
threats.description: With the security plugin disabled there is no user identity and no audit log on OpenSearch; changes to indices or the retention policy cannot be attributed.

threats.title: Indefinite retention of network metadata
threats.description: scripts/configure-retention-policy.sh creates an ISM delete policy and install.sh:configure_retention calls it with RETENTION_DAYS.
threats.mitigation: scripts/configure-retention-policy.sh (ISM policy); install.sh configure_retention. Retention does not cover pfblockerng-* unless the pattern is applied (NOT VERIFIED).

data.name: Grafana 12.3.0
data.description: Dashboards over OpenSearch datasources (dashboards/*.json, imported by setup.sh via HTTP API with basic auth). HTTP 3000, ufw open.

threats.title: Default Grafana admin credentials
threats.description: install.sh interactive_config falls back to password 'admin' when left empty and skips reset-admin-password in that case; config.env.example sets GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASS=admin and setup.sh defaults the same. Grafana is served over plain HTTP on 3000 (ufw allow 3000/tcp). Anyone reaching the port can sign in and read everything, add datasources or install plugins.
threats.mitigation: install.sh interactive_config generates a random password when the prompt is empty and rejects 'admin' via grafana_password_ok (scripts/lib-install-safety.sh); install_grafana sets it after first start and exits if grafana-cli fails. setup.sh refuses an empty or 'admin' GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASS; config.env.example no longer ships admin. Grafana 3000 is opened only to GRAFANA_ALLOWED_SOURCES (required) by firewall_plan. Plain HTTP remains (t_gf_tls). Existing installs with an admin password are not changed.

threats.title: Attacker-controlled event fields rendered in dashboards
threats.description: UNVERIFIED: dashboards display fields such as alert.signature, http hostnames and DNS queries that originate in attacker traffic (and, via the open UDP port, arbitrary senders). Whether any panel renders unescaped HTML was not checked.

data.name: OpenSearch indices
data.description: suricata-YYYY.MM.dd and pfblockerng-YYYY.MM.dd on the SIEM disk (/opt/opensearch/data). Index templates in config/opensearch-*.json.

threats.title: Sensitive network metadata exposed in cleartext
threats.description: Indices hold DNS names, URLs, SNI, internal IP addresses and GeoIP of users. Because of the open API (t_os_open) and plaintext transport (UDP forwarder, HTTP Telegraf output), anyone on the path or the network can read it. No at-rest encryption configured in repo.
threats.mitigation: Consequence of t_os_open: with OpenSearch on 127.0.0.1 and no ufw rule for 9200 (install.sh configure_firewall / firewall_plan), the indices are not readable from the network on a fresh install. Residual: a user with shell access on the SIEM host, anyone allowed through OPENSEARCH_BIND/OPENSEARCH_ALLOWED_SOURCES, and unauthenticated Grafana users via its datasource can still read them; transport is still cleartext.

data.name: config.env (secrets)
data.description: Operator-local file holding SIEM/pfSense addresses and GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASS, sourced as shell by setup.sh (source "$CONFIG_FILE") and ignored by git (.gitignore: config.env).

threats.title: Credentials committed to the repo
threats.description: config.env is in .gitignore; only config.env.example (placeholders, plus default 'admin' password) is tracked; .gitleaksignore lists reviewed false positives.
threats.mitigation: Mitigated against commit: .gitignore:45 config.env. The file is sourced as shell, so a tampered config.env on the operator machine would execute code (operator-local trust, accepted).

threats.title: Grafana credentials passed on curl command lines
threats.description: setup.sh uses curl -u "${GRAFANA_AUTH}" for datasource and dashboard API calls, which exposes the password to other local users via process listings on the operator machine for the duration of the call.
